provenance.notes: Hand-written example. The checks are real runs recorded on 2026-11-14 (logs in evidence/). The claims, refusals and routing are written by us to show the shape and are NOT model output.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

acceptanceCriteria.text: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member of a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly builds cleanly and gets a generated resolver.
The other trigger-matrix shapes (non-generic struct, generic or non-generic class, non-generic record struct) keep working as before.
No CS8785 or AD0001 warning is produced for these shapes.

claims.statusReason: Every named test ran with the outcome the claim needs: GenericsFormatterTests.ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference, GenericsFormatterTests.ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference.
claims.modelNote: The test compiles the library to real IL, fails on base source and passes on the AI commit. The two-project build from the issue was not run (CHK5).

claims.text: The other trigger-matrix shapes are unchanged by the patch.
claims.statusReason: A behaviour claim with no executed check behind it.
claims.modelNote: The existing 167 tests pass, but none is mapped to the four 'ok' matrix rows, and the diagnostic filter applies to every diagnostic. No check supports this claim.

claims.text: The new filter only removes diagnostics that could not be reported at a valid location anyway.
claims.statusReason: A named test had the opposite outcome from what the claim needs: GenericsFormatterTests.ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember in CHK4 (failed, expected passed).
claims.modelNote: With a crash-only fix the analyzer still reports MsgPack004 for an unkeyed member of a referenced type (with no source location). The filter removes it.

refusals.question: Should the consuming project stop reporting MsgPack004 and similar diagnostics for members of types from referenced assemblies?
refusals.whyAiRefused: The issue is silent. Dropping the diagnostic hides a real problem in a dependency, but keeping it can break a build over code the consumer cannot change. This is a policy decision for the maintainer.

refusals.question: Is the new README and MsgPack004.md text correct that the defining assembly reports these problems?
refusals.whyAiRefused: That holds only if the defining assembly runs the analyzer. A package built without it never reports them, and the AI cannot know that for consumers' dependencies.

outOfRequirement.description: The patch adds a filter that removes every diagnostic whose location is outside the compilation being analyzed. The issue asks only that the generator and analyzer stop crashing.
The patch adds user-facing documentation to README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md describing the new diagnostic behaviour. The issue does not request documentation.

unknowns.text: Only MsgPack004 was observed being dropped. Other diagnostics may be dropped too.
The two-project dotnet build repro from the issue has not been run (CHK5).
Tests ran once, on one machine, for net8.0 only.
The four trigger-matrix shapes that should be unchanged were not tested (CLM4).

A claim has no supporting evidence
The change goes beyond the requirement
The AI refused to decide something the human must
Some checks did not run (visible, not hidden)
